final_message:
I fixed `int_to_roman` in `src/roman.py`. It had no entries for the subtractive forms, so 4 came out as `IIII` and 9 as `VIIII`. Likewise 40 was `XXXX`, 90 was `LXXXX`, 400 was `CCCC` and 900 was `DCCCC`.

I added `CM`, `CD`, `XC`, `XL`, `IX` and `IV` to the value table. Now 1994 gives `MCMXCIV`, 4 gives `IV` and 49 gives `XLIX`. For every integer from 1 to 3999, `roman_to_int(int_to_roman(i))` returns `i`.

The repo has no git history and I didn't see a test suite, so I didn't add a test.
